definitions.explanation: The traditional craft of dyeing fabric using indigo plant extract, producing distinctive deep blue colors. Also refers to the fabric or products dyed by this method.

examples.japanese: {藍染|あいぞ}めの{手|て}ぬぐいを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought an indigo-dyed tenugui towel.

examples.japanese: {藍染|あいぞ}め{体験|たいけん}ができる{工房|こうぼう}を{訪|たず}ねた。
examples.english: I visited a workshop where you can try indigo dyeing.

examples.japanese: {徳島県|とくしまけん}は{藍染|あいぞ}めの{産地|さんち}として{知|し}られ、{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}から{続|つづ}く{伝統|でんとう}がある。
examples.english: Tokushima Prefecture is known as a center of indigo dyeing, with a tradition dating back to the Edo period.

notes:
{藍|あい} (indigo) is one of the most iconic colors in Japanese textile tradition. The deep blue color produced by indigo dyeing was so prevalent in Edo-period Japan that foreign visitors called it "Japan blue." The dyeing process involves fermenting indigo leaves and repeatedly dipping fabric to build up layers of color.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {藍染|あいぞ}めの{布|ぬの}: indigo-dyed cloth
- {藍染|あいぞ}め{体験|たいけん}: indigo dyeing experience/workshop
- {藍染|あいぞ}め{製品|せいひん}: indigo-dyed products
- {天然|てんねん}{藍染|あいぞ}め: natural indigo dyeing (as opposed to synthetic)

RELATED TERMS:
- {藍|あい}: indigo (the plant or the color)
- {染|そ}め{物|もの}: dyeing, dyed goods — the broader category of textile dyeing
- {絞|しぼ}り{染|ぞ}め: tie-dyeing — another traditional Japanese dyeing technique
- {草木染|くさきぞ}め: plant dyeing — dyeing with various natural plant materials
